name: fork()
description: Creates a new process by duplicating the calling process. The child process is an exact copy of the parent, sharing copy-on-write page tables, duplicated file descriptors, and signal handlers. The kernel allocates a new task_struct, pid, and kernel stack, then integrates the child into the scheduler runqueue.

main_flow.title: User Space — fork() / clone() call
main_flow.description: The user-space program invokes fork() (or the lower-level clone() system call). The C library wrapper issues the syscall instruction, transitioning from ring 3 to ring 0. On x86-64, this uses the SYSCALL instruction which stores the return address in RCX and RFLAGS in R11 before jumping to the kernel entry point.

detail_nodes.title: glibc fork() wrapper
detail_nodes.description: The glibc fork() function calls the clone() syscall with flags SIGCHLD, setting up the arguments for the kernel. It invokes the syscall instruction (or int 0x80 on x86-32) to trigger the transition into kernel mode. The syscall number for fork on x86 is 57 (x86-64) or 2 (x86-32).

detail_nodes.title: SYSCALL / int 0x80 instruction
detail_nodes.description: The CPU executes the SYSCALL instruction which atomically saves RIP/RFLAGS, switches the stack pointer to the kernel stack defined in the TSS, and jumps to the MSR_LSTAR entry point (system_call in entry_64.S). The hardware then runs in ring 0 with the kernel's GS base.

main_flow.title: Kernel Entry — syscall dispatch → sys_fork → do_fork
main_flow.description: The kernel's syscall dispatch table routes the syscall number to sys_fork() (x86-32) or stub_clone() (x86-64). These architecture-specific stubs gather register arguments and call the architecture-independent do_fork() function in kernel/fork.c, which performs the actual process duplication logic.

detail_nodes.title: sys_fork() / sys_clone() entry
detail_nodes.description: On x86-32, sys_fork() is defined in arch/x86/kernel/process.c. It calls do_fork() with clone flags SIGCHLD, passing the user-space stack pointer from the pt_regs structure. On x86-64, stub_clone() collects the register arguments and delegates to sys_clone(), which also calls do_fork().

detail_nodes.title: do_fork() entry point
detail_nodes.description: do_fork() in kernel/fork.c is the central fork implementation. It validates clone flags for consistency, then calls copy_process() to duplicate the parent's task_struct and all associated resources. After copy_process() returns, do_fork() calls wake_up_new_task() to schedule the child.

source_ref.snippet:
long do_fork(unsigned long clone_flags,
  unsigned long stack_start,
  struct pt_regs *regs,
  unsigned long stack_size,
  int __user *parent_tidptr,
  int __user *child_tidptr)

detail_nodes.title: CLONE_* flags
detail_nodes.description: The clone_flags parameter controls what resources are shared between parent and child. CLONE_VM shares the address space (used by threads), CLONE_FILES shares file descriptors, CLONE_SIGHAND shares signal handlers. A plain fork() uses only SIGCHLD as the flags value, resulting in full duplication of all resources.

main_flow.title: Process Duplication — copy_process → dup_task_struct → new task_struct
main_flow.description: copy_process() is the heart of fork: it calls dup_task_struct() to allocate a new task_struct and kernel stack, copies or shares each process resource (memory map, file descriptors, signal handlers) depending on clone_flags, initializes scheduling fields, and assigns a new PID via alloc_pid().

detail_nodes.title: copy_process() orchestration
detail_nodes.description: copy_process() in kernel/fork.c is the comprehensive function that duplicates a process. It validates flag combinations, calls dup_task_struct() first, then proceeds to copy each subsystem (creds, mm, files, signals, etc.). It initializes the new task's list linkage and returns a pointer to the child task_struct on success.

source_ref.snippet:
static struct task_struct *copy_process(unsigned long clone_flags,
  unsigned long stack_start,
  struct pt_regs *regs,
  unsigned long stack_size,
  int __user *child_tidptr,
  struct pid *pid,
  int trace)

detail_nodes.title: dup_task_struct() — new task_struct + kernel stack
detail_nodes.description: dup_task_struct() allocates a new task_struct with alloc_task_struct() and a new 8KB (THREAD_SIZE) kernel stack with alloc_thread_info(). It then does a plain struct copy of the parent task_struct into the new one, and sets up the thread_info pointer to point at the bottom of the new kernel stack.

detail_nodes.title: task_struct field initialization
detail_nodes.description: After dup_task_struct() copies the parent's fields, copy_process() reinitializes fields that must be unique per process: the PID, state (set to TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE), usage count, list heads for children/siblings, CPU time accounting, and the thread_struct for register state including the instruction pointer set to ret_from_fork.

detail_nodes.title: alloc_pid() — new PID assignment
detail_nodes.description: alloc_pid() in kernel/pid.c allocates a new struct pid from the pidmap bitmap. The kernel maintains separate PID namespaces; alloc_pid() finds the next free PID number in each applicable namespace, allocates a struct pid object, and attaches it to the new task_struct via the task's pids[] array.

main_flow.title: Memory & Resources — copy_mm (CoW page tables) → copy_files → copy_sighand
main_flow.description: copy_process() duplicates memory mappings and other resources controlled by clone_flags. For a plain fork(), copy_mm() calls dup_mm() which duplicates the mm_struct and marks all writable pages copy-on-write in both parent and child page tables. copy_files() clones the file descriptor table, and copy_sighand() duplicates signal handler state.

detail_nodes.title: copy_mm() — address space duplication
detail_nodes.description: copy_mm() checks CLONE_VM: if set (threads), the child shares the parent's mm_struct. Otherwise, it calls dup_mm() to allocate a new mm_struct, copy all vm_area_struct VMAs via dup_mmap(), and walk all page table entries calling copy_page_range() to set PTEs as read-only and mark them copy-on-write for both parent and child.

detail_nodes.title: copy_page_range() — CoW PTE setup
detail_nodes.description: copy_page_range() in mm/memory.c walks the parent's page tables (PGD→PUD→PMD→PTE) and for each present, writable PTE, clears the write bit in both parent and child and increments the page reference count. This implements copy-on-write: a page fault on either process later will call do_wp_page() to create a private copy.

detail_nodes.title: copy_files() — file descriptor table clone
detail_nodes.description: copy_files() checks CLONE_FILES: if set (threads), the child increments the reference count of the parent's files_struct and shares it. Otherwise, dup_fd() allocates a new files_struct, copies the fdtable with all open file pointers, and increments struct file reference counts for each open descriptor.

detail_nodes.title: copy_sighand() — signal handler duplication
detail_nodes.description: copy_sighand() checks CLONE_SIGHAND: if set, the child shares the parent's sighand_struct (reference counted). Otherwise, it allocates a new sighand_struct and copies the parent's sigaction array with all signal handler function pointers and flags. copy_signal() also duplicates the signal_struct for pending signals and session/group info.

main_flow.title: Scheduler Integration — sched_fork → wake_up_new_task → runqueue
main_flow.description: Before the child can run, it must be integrated into the CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler). sched_fork() initializes the child's sched_entity and places it on a runqueue. wake_up_new_task() then marks the child TASK_RUNNING and enqueues it on the CPU's runqueue, making it eligible for scheduling.

detail_nodes.title: sched_fork() — scheduling entity init
detail_nodes.description: sched_fork() in kernel/sched.c initializes the child's sched_entity (se) embedded in task_struct. It sets the child's scheduling policy, priority (inherited from parent), and initializes the CFS virtual runtime (vruntime). The task state is set to TASK_RUNNING but it is not yet enqueued on any runqueue.

detail_nodes.title: struct sched_entity initialization
detail_nodes.description: The sched_entity (p->se) inside the child's task_struct is initialized with vruntime set to max(parent_vruntime, cfs_rq->min_vruntime) to prevent the new task from monopolizing the CPU by starting with an unfairly low virtual time. The load weight is set based on the task's nice value.

detail_nodes.title: wake_up_new_task() — enqueue on runqueue
detail_nodes.description: wake_up_new_task() in kernel/sched.c is called from do_fork() after copy_process() completes. It acquires the runqueue lock, calls activate_task() → enqueue_task() to insert the child's sched_entity into the CFS red-black tree, and may trigger a reschedule if the child has higher priority than the current task.

main_flow.title: Return — parent gets child PID; child begins at ret_from_fork
main_flow.description: do_fork() returns the child's PID to the parent process, which resumes execution after the fork() call with the child PID as the return value. The child process begins execution at ret_from_fork in arch/x86/kernel/entry_64.S, which returns 0 to user space, making fork() return twice — once in each process.

detail_nodes.title: Parent returns child PID
detail_nodes.description: copy_process() returns the child task_struct pointer to do_fork(). do_fork() extracts the PID number using task_pid_vnr() and returns it. The kernel syscall exit path restores the parent's registers (with RAX set to the child PID) and executes SYSRET to return to user space with the child PID as fork()'s return value.

detail_nodes.title: Child resumes at ret_from_fork with return value 0
detail_nodes.description: The child task_struct's thread.ip was set to ret_from_fork during copy_process(). When the scheduler first runs the child, it jumps to ret_from_fork in entry_64.S. This assembly stub calls schedule_tail() to release the runqueue lock, then calls the user-space return path with RAX=0, so fork() returns 0 in the child.

source_ref.snippet:
ENTRY(ret_from_fork)
  DEFAULT_FRAME
  push kernel_eflags(%rip)
  CFI_ADJUST_CFA_OFFSET 8
  popf
  CFI_ADJUST_CFA_OFFSET -8
  call schedule_tail

detail_nodes.title: Child's fork() return value: 0
detail_nodes.description: By convention, fork() returns 0 in the child process. This is achieved by copy_process() zeroing the child's pt_regs.ax field (the syscall return value register) during task_struct initialization. When the child eventually reaches the syscall return path, it finds RAX=0 and returns that to user space.
